definition: Positive motivation is a favorable motivational response toward a stimulus, reflected in stronger liking and a greater tendency to mentally and behaviorally approach it. In this source, it refers specifically to adults’ increased positive responses to infant faces.

reasons: The first sentence gives a general definition of “positive motivation” as a favorable motivational response involving liking and mental/behavioral approach, but the packet only supports a study-specific use tied to adults’ motivational responses to infant faces; it does not provide that broader definitional meaning.

The packet supports infant-face-specific positive/approach motivation in adults, but not the full generalized phrasing about “a stimulus” or the specific claims about “mental” approach and “behavioral” approach as a dictionary definition.

The definition’s general phrasing (“greater tendency to mentally and behaviorally approach it”) is not explicitly supported by the packet text; the packet reports enhanced liking/representational/evoked responses but does not describe “mentally and behaviorally approach” as the operational meaning of positive motivation.

“Positive motivation is a favorable motivational response toward a stimulus” is not directly defined in the packet; the packet discusses motivational responses/enhancement for infant faces but does not provide this as a definitional characterization of the term.

The packet does support that the study’s relevant effects involve adults’ increased positive motivational responses (liking/evoked/representational) to infant faces after secure-attachment priming, but the definition’s broader first sentence contains unsupported claims.
